proposals.current: Allows to filter/remove specific ROI metadata entries
proposals.proposed: Removes or filters specific metadata entries from the 2D ROI list.

proposals.current: Creates a color image in which the 2D ROIs from the input image's overlay are drawn over the image. It takes an ImageJ image and produces a color ImageJ image, applying the selected outline, fill, label, opacity, and magnification settings.
proposals.proposed: Renders the 2D ROIs drawn on the input image's overlay into a new color image. It takes an ImageJ image and produces a color ImageJ image, applying the selected outline, fill, label, opacity, and magnification settings.

proposals.current: Rotates all ROI in the ROI list. A newer algorithm that allows to do scaling/rotating/translation in one is available. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Rotates all 2D ROI in the ROI list (this is the old variant). A newer algorithm that allows to do scaling/rotating/translation in one is available.

proposals.current: Scales all ROI in the ROI list. If you want to have more flexibility, use one of the 'Change ROI properties' nodes. A newer algorithm that allows to do scaling/rotating/translation in one is available.
proposals.proposed: Scales all 2D ROI in the ROI list (this is the old variant). If you want to have more flexibility, use one of the 'Change ROI properties' nodes. A newer algorithm that allows to do scaling/rotating/translation in one is available.

proposals.current: Associates an image to the ROI. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Sets the image associated with each 2D ROI.

proposals.current: Sets ROI metadata by statistics. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Sets 2D ROI metadata by statistics, with each value computed via a user-written expression.

proposals.current: Sets the ROI metadata (property map) from a table. The table either has a column that indicates the ROI index or contains one row per ROI (row index is the ROI index) This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Sets the 2D ROI metadata (property map) from a table. The table either has a column that indicates the ROI index or contains one row per ROI (row index is the ROI index)

proposals.current: Sets properties of all Roi to values extracted from annotations.
proposals.proposed: Sets properties of all 2D ROI to values extracted from annotations.

proposals.current: Sets properties of all ROI to values extracted from a table. Table rows are matched to their ROI and the column values are put into expression variables, so the ROI can be modified. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Sets properties of all 2D ROI to values extracted from a table. Table rows are matched to their ROI and the column values are put into expression variables, so the ROI can be modified.

proposals.current: Sorts a ROI list according to an expression-defined property. Has access to annotations and measurements. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Sorts a 2D ROI list according to an expression-defined property. Has access to annotations and measurements.

proposals.current: Algorithm that extracts connected components across one or multiple dimensions. The output consists of multiple ROI lists, one for each connected component. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Splits each 2D ROI into its connected components across one or multiple dimensions. The output consists of multiple ROI lists, one for each connected component.

proposals.current: Converts the ROI into point ROI that are the centroids of their inputs
proposals.proposed: Outlines each 2D ROI as a point ROI placed at the centroid of its input.

proposals.current: Applies rotation, scaling, and translation of 2D ROI. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Transforms each 2D ROI by applying rotation, scaling, and translation.

proposals.current: Removes any association of the ROI from any image.
proposals.proposed: Clears any association of each 2D ROI from any image.

proposals.current: Performs segmentation via watershed on a 2D or 3D image using flooding simulations. Please note that this node returns labels instead of masks. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Performs the classic watershed segmentation on a 2D or 3D image using flooding simulations. Please note that this node returns labels instead of masks.

proposals.current: Applies a 3x3 sharpening filter. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Applies a 3x3 Laplacian sharpening filter to the image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

This node supports the calculation of both the minimum and maximum thresholds.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Implements a custom min+max auto threshold on 16-bit images via a user-written expression. This node supports the calculation of both the minimum and maximum thresholds.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Applies a mathematical operation to each pixel to convert the color into a greyscale value.
proposals.proposed: Applies a custom auto threshold to color images by evaluating a user-written expression on each pixel's color components.

proposals.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. This node supports various methods: Mean (threshold is mean local pixel value) Median (threshold is median local pixel value) MidGray (threshold is average of min and max pixel values) Otsu (threshold is the local otsu threshold) If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.
proposals.proposed: Applies a local auto threshold to 8-bit greyscale images. This node supports various methods: Mean (threshold is mean local pixel value) Median (threshold is median local pixel value) MidGray (threshold is average of min and max pixel values) Otsu (threshold is the local otsu threshold) If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.

This node supports various methods: Mean (threshold is mean local pixel value) Median (threshold is median local pixel value) MidGray (threshold is average of min and max pixel values) Otsu (threshold is the local otsu threshold) If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Applies a local auto threshold to 16-bit greyscale images. This node supports various methods: Mean (threshold is mean local pixel value) Median (threshold is median local pixel value) MidGray (threshold is average of min and max pixel values) Otsu (threshold is the local otsu threshold) If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. Bernsen recommends a radius of 15 and a contrast threshold of 15.
proposals.proposed: Applies the local Bernsen auto threshold to 16-bit images. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. Bernsen recommends a radius of 15 and a contrast threshold of 15.

proposals.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. Based on a simple contrast toggle. This procedure does not have user-provided parameters other than the kernel radius. Sets the pixel value to either white or black depending on whether its current value is closest to the local Max or Min respectively. The procedure is similar to Toggle Contrast Enhancement (see Soille, Morphological Image Analysis (2004), p. 259
proposals.proposed: Applies the local contrast auto threshold on 16-bit images. Based on a simple contrast toggle. No parameters other than the kernel radius. Sets the pixel to white or black depending on whether its value is closest to the local Max or Min, similar to Toggle Contrast Enhancement (Soille, Morphological Image Analysis (2004), p. 259). If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Applies the local Niblack auto threshold to 16-bit images. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. The threshold is calculated as t = mean * (1 + p * exp(-q * mean) + k * ((stdev / r) - 1)). If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Applies the local Phansalkar auto threshold to 16-bit images. The threshold is calculated as t = mean * (1 + p * exp(-q * mean) + k * ((stdev / r) - 1)). If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.
proposals.proposed: Applies the local Niblack auto threshold to 8-bit images. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.

proposals.current: Thresholds the image with a manual threshold. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Thresholds the 16-bit image with a manual threshold. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Thresholds the image with a manual threshold. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Thresholds the 32-bit image with a manual threshold. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Thresholds LAB images.
proposals.proposed: Manually thresholds a color image in the LAB color space, using a minimum and maximum value for each channel.

proposals.current: Thresholds the image with a threshold calculated from the image pixel values (percentile of the 65536-bin histogram). If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Thresholds the 16-bit image with a percentile of the 65536-bin histogram of the image pixel values. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Thresholds the image with a threshold calculated from the image pixel values. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Applies an 8-bit percentile threshold calculated from the image pixel values. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Crops the incoming images to fit into the boundaries defined by the ROI. Alternative: Extract to ROI This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Crops each incoming image to the boundaries defined by its 2D ROI. Alternative: Extract to ROI

proposals.current: Makes all images within a iteration step have the same size by padding with the predefined background color according to the largest image dimensions. If you want more control (source/target) and/or also want to do the same for Z/C/T, use 'Equalize hyperstack dimensions' This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
proposals.proposed: Makes all 2D images from a single input the same size by padding with the predefined background color according to the largest image dimensions. If you want more control (source/target) and/or also want to do the same for Z/C/T, use 'Equalize hyperstack dimensions'

proposals.current: Pads each image slice with a background color. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Expands the canvas of each 2D image by padding the image with a background color.

proposals.current: The two endpoints of a line a provided via expressions. The resulting line is used as axis to mirror the image pixels. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Mirrors the image over a line whose two endpoints are provided via expressions. The resulting line is used as axis to mirror the image pixels. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: The two endpoints of a line a provided via one or multiple line ROI. If multiple ROI are provided, the algorithm is executed per ROI. If a ROI is not a line ROI, a line outline/hull operation is applied to the ROI (see Outline 2D ROI).The resulting line is used as axis to mirror the image pixels. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Mirrors the image over a line defined by one or multiple line ROI. If multiple ROI are provided, the algorithm runs per ROI. If a ROI is not a line ROI, a line outline/hull operation is applied (see Outline 2D ROI). The resulting line is the axis to mirror the image pixels. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Rotates the image by any kind of angle. Expands the canvas if necessary. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Rotates the 2D image by any free angle. Expands the canvas if necessary. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Aligns slices in the input image to other slices using methods implemented by TurboReg and MultiStackReg. Due to the variation in registration tasks, this node follows a 'rules' approach where each slice of the input image is matched to one rule that determines how the slice is aligned. There are three modes: (1) register to a reference slice, (2) use the same transformation calculated for another slice, and (3) apply no registration. Use the examples provided via the 'Tools' menu (top right of the parameter window) to get started with configuring the rules. Handling of RGB images: as the underlying alignment methods were only designed for greyscale images, RGB slices are automatically converted to greyscale prior to registration (using ImageJ methods). The resulting transformation is then applied per RGB channel, which is then output. Please note that if an RGB image is present, the output will be RGB. You may lose greyscale precision (16 bit/ 32 bit) in other slices. To prevent this, convert RGB to greyscale prior to registration (e.g. by splitting RGB channels into hyperstack channels). This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Registers 2D images slice by slice using the simple TurboReg and MultiStackReg rules approach: each slice is matched to a rule that aligns it to a reference slice, to another slice's computed transformation, or not at all. Configure the rules via the 'Tools' menu examples. RGB slices are converted to greyscale before registration and the transformation applied per RGB channel, so an RGB output stays RGB. Pre-convert RGB to greyscale to avoid losing 16-bit/32-bit precision in other slices.

proposals.current: Subtracts a blurred copy of the image and rescales the image to obtain the same contrast of large (low-frequency) structures as in the input image. This is equivalent to adding a high-pass filtered image and thus sharpens the image. "Radius (Sigma)" is the standard deviation (blur radius) of the Gaussian blur that is subtracted. "Mask Weight" determines the strength of filtering, where "Mask Weight"=1 would be an infinite weight of the high-pass filtered image that is added. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Sharpens the 2D image using unsharp masking. This is equivalent to adding a high-pass filtered image and thus sharpens the image. "Radius (Sigma)" is the standard deviation (blur radius) of the Gaussian blur that is subtracted. "Mask Weight" determines the strength of filtering, where "Mask Weight"=1 would be an infinite weight of the high-pass filtered image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Exports incoming images into a non-JIPipe format (PNG, JPEG, BMP, AVI, TIFF). Please note support for input images depending on the file format: PNG, JPEG, BMP: 2D images only AVI: 2D or 3D images only TIFF: All images supported This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed:
Exports the incoming images into the output directory in a non-JIPipe format (PNG, JPEG, BMP, AVI, TIFF). Please note support for input images depending on the file format:
  • PNG, JPEG, BMP: 2D images only
  • AVI: 2D or 3D images only
  • TIFF: All images supported

proposals.current: Annotates data with metadata extracted from OME metadata This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Annotates the data with metadata extracted from the OME image metadata.

proposals.current: Applies thresholding by applying a background subtraction, auto thresholding, and various morphological operations. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. If you want to further customize all steps, create a group or set of nodes that apply the following operations: Subtract background (rolling ball): default radius = 20 Auto threshold 2D Morphological dilation Morphological hole filling Morphological erosion Optional: Gaussian blur
proposals.proposed:
Segments bright spots in the 2D image by applying a background subtraction, auto thresholding, and various morphological operations. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
To customize all steps, chain these nodes: Subtract background (rolling ball, radius = 20), Auto threshold 2D, Morphological dilation, Morphological hole filling, Morphological erosion, and optional Gaussian blur.

proposals.current: Finds circular 2D objects via a Hough transform. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Detects circles in the 2D image via a Hough transform. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
